title: Leray's acyclicity lemma: a left exact functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms between bounded-below complexes of acyclic objects
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], where $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives (every object of $\mathcal A$ admits a monomorphism into an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]), and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with right derived functors $R^qF$ computed by injective resolutions. Let $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $a\in\mathbf Z$ an integer with $K^n=0$ and $L^n=0$ for all $n<a$, such that every term $K^n$ and every term $L^n$ is $F$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], i.e. $R^qF(K^n)=0$ and $R^qF(L^n)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all $n$. Let $\varphi:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism (a morphism of complexes with $H^r(\varphi)$ an isomorphism for every $r\in\mathbf Z$). Then the morphism of complexes $F(\varphi):F(K^\bullet)\to F(L^\bullet)$ of $\mathcal B$, obtained by applying $F$ termwise ($F(K^\bullet)^n=F(K^n)$ with differentials $F(d_K^n)$), is a quasi-isomorphism: $H^r(F(\varphi)):H^r(F(K^\bullet))\to H^r(F(L^\bullet))$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal B$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity, line 5717: a bounded below complex $A^\bullet$ of right $F$-acyclic objects computes $RF$, i.e. $F(A^\bullet)\to RF(A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathcal B)$), with Proposition 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics, line 5810) for $RF$ everywhere defined on $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and Lemma 015C (lemma-F-acyclic, line 5619) (2) for right $F$-acyclic = $R^qF=0$ for $q>0$ when $F$ is left exact. The statement here is the form in complexes: applying 015E to $K^\bullet$ and to $L^\bullet$, $F(\varphi)$ is identified with the isomorphism $RF(\varphi)$ of $D^+(\mathcal B)$ through the natural transformation $F\to RF$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism.
